annotations.text:
Spark first-launch flow

Terminal: `curl … | sh` installs the CLI, runs preflight, pulls the compose bundle, starts the stack, prints the setup URL. No terminal prompts.

Browser: /setup wizard (this canvas), 8 steps, ~10 min. Left rail = progress, right = one decision per screen. Every step has a "connected" state and a fix-it path; nothing degrades silently.

After Launch: /ready with three in-product walkthroughs.

Rules baked into the copy

• No fallbacks: a down provider is reported, never substituted.
• Credentials encrypted at rest with a per-machine key; OAuth/device-code preferred over pasted tokens.
• Sign-in off by default on LAN, with a visible warning and a later path.
• Everything editable later in Settings; the wizard never becomes the only way.

Open questions for Jozef

1. Model list: show only what fits, or everything with a "does not fit" state?
2. Should Launch also start a resident (Muninn-style) by default, or leave that to tutorial 3?
3. Is "Host process" runtime worth offering on Spark at all?
4. GitHub App vs PAT as the first-class path (App needs a published app on GitHub).
